text: David again gathered all the chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand in all.
Then David and all the people with him set out from Baale-judah to bring up from there the ark of God, which is called by the Name, the name of the LORD of hosts, who is enthroned above the cherubim.
They set the ark of God on a new cart and carried it from the house of Abinadab on the hill. Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, were guiding the new cart,
bringing it with the ark of God from the house of Abinadab on the hill, and Ahio walked ahead of the ark.
David and the whole house of Israel were celebrating before the LORD with all kinds of instruments of cypress wood—with lyres, harps, tambourines, rattles, and cymbals.

versions.text: David and the whole house of Israel celebrated before the LORD with all their might, with songs and with lyres, harps, tambourines, rattles, and cymbals.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew reads "with all [instruments of] cypress wood" (bekhol atzei veroshim). "With all their might, with songs" follows the parallel account in Chronicles rather than the Hebrew text here. If the alternate reading is retained, it should at least be marked with a footnote; otherwise render the Hebrew as it stands.

text: When they came to the threshing floor of Nacon, Uzzah reached out to the ark of God and took hold of it, because the oxen had stumbled.
The anger of the LORD blazed against Uzzah, and God struck him down there for his irreverence, and he died there beside the ark of God.

versions.text: The anger of the LORD blazed out against Uzzah, and God struck him down there for his irreverence, and he died there beside the ark of God.
versions.explanation: "Blazed out" is an awkward collocation when read aloud; "blazed against" (or "burned against") is smoother and matches the idiom.

text: David was angry because the LORD had broken out against Uzzah, so he named that place Perez-uzzah, and it is called so to this day.

versions.text: David was angry because the LORD had broken out against Uzzah, and that place is called Perez-uzzah to this day.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has an active naming ("he called that place"), which the current rendering flattens into a passive statement, losing David's act of naming.

text: David was afraid of the LORD that day, and he said, "How can the ark of the LORD ever come to me?"
So David was unwilling to bring the ark of the LORD up to himself in the City of David; instead he turned it aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.
The ark of the LORD remained in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite three months, and the LORD blessed Obed-edom and his entire household.

King David was told, "The LORD has blessed the house of Obed-edom and all that belongs to him because of the ark of God." So David went and brought the ark of God up from the house of Obed-edom to the City of David with rejoicing.
When those carrying the ark of the LORD had taken six steps, David sacrificed a bull and a fattened calf.

versions.text: When those carrying the ark of the LORD had taken six steps, he sacrificed a bull and a fattened calf.
versions.explanation: The pronoun "he" is ambiguous after the plural "those carrying the ark"; naming David (the implied subject) makes the sentence clear for a listener.

text: And David danced before the LORD with all his might, wearing a linen ephod.
So David and the whole house of Israel brought up the ark of the LORD with shouting and the sound of the ram's horn.

As the ark of the LORD entered the City of David, Michal daughter of Saul looked down through the window, and when she saw King David leaping and dancing before the LORD, she despised him in her heart.
They brought in the ark of the LORD and set it in its place inside the tent David had pitched for it, and David offered burnt offerings and fellowship offerings before the LORD.
When David had finished offering the burnt offerings and the fellowship offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD of hosts.
He distributed to all the people, to the whole multitude of Israel, both men and women, a loaf of bread, a portion of meat, and a cake of raisins to each one. Then all the people went home.

When David returned to bless his household, Michal daughter of Saul came out to meet him and said, "How the king of Israel has distinguished himself today, exposing himself before the eyes of his servants' slave girls as one of the vulgar might shamelessly expose himself!"
David said to Michal, "It was before the LORD, who chose me over your father and all his house and appointed me ruler over the LORD's people, over Israel—before the LORD I will celebrate.
I will make myself even more contemptible than this, and I will be humbled in my own eyes. But by the slave girls you spoke of, by them I will be held in honor."
And Michal daughter of Saul had no child to the day of her death.
